mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is held constant above 5% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 forward 60-day return tends to be negative due to persistent discounting of growth prospects.
failure_condition: In high-rate regimes, 60-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05) or the rate remains below 5% for the next 60 days, reversing the signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) coinciding with rising consumer confidence (HOUST) predicts a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days as market anticipates sustained wage growth.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 2% month-over-month and HOUST rises by > 5% month-over-month
failure_condition: No significant correlation between PAYEMS and HOUST changes and SPX 20-day returns (Pearson < 0.2) or the signal reverses in the next 20 days.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 2% suggests weakening supply-side constraints, which tends to drive a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 days as demand reallocation occurs.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by > 2% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: INDPRO recovers by > 2% in the following month or SPX 5-day returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) unexpectedly rises by more than 0.5% in a month, the S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days is typically negative due to anticipated inflationary pressure and rate hike expectations.
failure_condition: Inflation surprise months, 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) or CPIAUCSL reverts within 2 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in unemployment (UNRATE) below 3.5% for three consecutive months triggers a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 days as markets anticipate further monetary easing.
failure_condition: UNRATE remains below 3.5% for more than 6 months without a positive SPX 60-day return, or the 60-day return is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in payrolls (PAYEMS) and consumer sentiment (HOUST) above their 2023 Q4 averages are associated with a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days as market anticipates robust economic momentum.
failure_condition: No significant positive return in the next 20 days (p > 0.05) or proxies revert to 2023 Q4 averages within 10 days.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in industrial production (INDPRO) followed by a rebound of greater than 3% in the same month predicts a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 days due to market anticipation of supply disruptions persisting into the near term.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by > 4% in a month and rebounds by > 3% in the same month
failure_condition: 5-day forward return is not significantly negative (p > 0.05) or INDPRO does not show the described pattern.

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate remains unchanged for four consecutive months during a recession (as defined by GDP < potential), the S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days is typically positive as markets price in the likelihood of policy easing.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 < potential and FEDFUNDS unchanged for four months
failure_condition: In such regimes, 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) or GDP recovers without a policy shift.
